newsitem.title: UK: Go-Ahead says wins Thames rail franchise.
newsitem.headline: Go-Ahead says wins Thames rail franchise.

text.p: Urban bus operator Go-Ahead Group Plc said on Thursday that Victory Railway Holdings, in which it has a 65 percent stake, had been awarded the Thames Trains franchise by the UK's director of passenger rail franchising.
It said the franchise award was for an initial period of approximately seven and a half years.

Thames Trains operates rail services between London's Paddington station and Oxford, via Maidenhead and Reading. Some of the services extend to Hereford in the west of England via Worcester and to Stratford-upon-Avon.
It also runs services between Gatwick Airport and Reading.

Go-Ahead said its strategy was to focus on urban passenger transport. Under the term of the franchise award, which slots into Go-Ahead's strategic aims, Victory will buy Thames Trains for a nominal consideration.

Under the franchising agreement it will receive a subsidy starting at 31.7 million stg for the the first full year to March 31 1998, reducing to no subsidy by March 31 2004. The subsidy averages 16.4 million per annum.
The Thames Trains franchise is seen as earnings-enhancing in the current financial year. Capital required to meet the franchise obligation is 4.25 million stg.
Go-Ahead is financing 4.18 million of the capital required. This capital will comprise of a loan note of 4.05 million and a share subscription of 130,000 stg.
The bus operator will also provide a performance bond of 4.25 million stg.

Go-Ahead said in order to finance all these faciltiies it has revised bank facilities and will also place 2.277 million new ordinary shares with institutional investors priced at 305 pence per share. Go-Ahead shares are currently trading up 16 1/2 pence at 334.
